text:
incident-bot: PAGER -> Critical: Customer 'Arbor Finance' (private VPC) reporting 504s on API ingress via NLB in eu-west-1. Affected: dedicated/private pool, multiple tenants seeing 502/504. Paging oncall.

claire: I'm on it, picking up the page. Collecting impact details from monitoring now.

raj: saw spike in 5xx from the NLB target group healthcheck failing. Root cause unclear yet — could be SG or healthcheck backend. tagging @maria for infra/sg

maria: oncall infra. I can access the customer's VPC in the private control plane. Quick check: NLB healthchecks are failing from our probe IPs, clients behind ALB are healthy. Looks like the NLB->backend path is being interrupted.

sam: customer-reported that this started after a scheduled security hardening from their side around 03:12 UTC. They opened a support ticket claiming SG change. We should treat it as potential SG deny.

claire: good signal. Maria, can you confirm NLB healthcheck source IPs and show which SG rules would allow them? Also grab target group health status.

maria: pulling target group:```\naws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456:targetgroup/arb-api/abcd1234\n```
returns 10/10 unhealthy, reason: TCP connection refused from healthcheck source 10.200.50.5

maria: NLB healthcheck source list per our docs for private deployments: 10.200.50.0/24 and 10.200.60.0/24 (control plane probes). Customer's SG currently allows 10.200.60.0/24 but not 10.200.50.0/24 — looks like one of the probe ranges got dropped.

raj: that matches the timing of their change. They probably replaced a permissive rule with a narrower one and missed the 50 range.

claire: can we do a rapid mitigation? Options: 1) ask customer to re-add 10.200.50.0/24 to SG (fastest), 2) temporarily route traffic to failover dedicated pool in another AZ/region if available, 3) change NLB healthcheck to use source in 10.200.60.0/24 (risky / config change).

ops-lead: escalate to customer success to coordinate with their network team; we should not change healthcheck config without customer's consent. Option 1 is preferred.

claire: @olivia can you ping CS to get customer network contact and confirm they rolled out a change at 03:12? We need an ETA for SG rollback.

olivia: pinged CS and the customer's network ops. They confirm the change, will try to reapply the missing CIDR. ETA 12-15 min. "Rolling back a couple of rules now." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

incident-bot: Automated note: rolling timeline started. Noted impacted customers: Arbor Finance. Initiated priority page at 03:18 UTC.

maria: while we wait, I can open an emergency inbound rule on our side by pushing a temporary policy to allow probe from 10.200.50.0/24 to the target ENIs, but need approval since this touches security posture.

claire: approve temporary patch if it gets customers back quickly — must be timeboxed and reverted after customer confirms. @ops-lead approve?

ops-lead: approve. Timebox to 30 minutes, document change and revert plan. Notify audit.

maria: applying patch now:```\n# attach temporary SG rule to target ENIs\naws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abcd1234 --protocol tcp --port 8080 --cidr 10.200.50.0/24 --description "temp allow nlb probe - incident 3825000000"\n```

maria: rule applied. Healthchecks started to show passing within 30s.

raj: monitoring shows target group healthy -> %healthy went 0 -> 100 in 40s. Client 504s falling back. Grafana alert cleared for 504 spike.

claire: customer CS confirms rollback completed on their side as well. They reapplied the 10.200.50.0/24 rule at 03:28 UTC.

olivia: CS confirms customer will keep both probe ranges for 24h and then coordinate a safe hardening window with Redwood.

maria: reverting our temporary SG change now to avoid drift:```\naws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abcd1234 --protocol tcp --port 8080 --cidr 10.200.50.0/24\n```
Revert completed.

claire: verifying final state... target group remains healthy after revert. Customer traffic stable. No further 5xx alerts for 12+ minutes.

sam: adding post-incident action: update docs + control plane validators to flag missing probe range during security-harden windows. Also reach out to customers with recommended SG ruleset for NLB probes.

ops-lead: agree. Also propose a preflight check in the console that warns if a customer's planned SG change would drop required probe CIDRs.

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> status: mitigated. Root cause: customer SG change removed required NLB probe CIDR (10.200.50.0/24). Time to mitigation ~10-15 minutes via temporary SG patch and customer rollback. Actions: CS follow-up, doc updates, control plane preflight.

claire: thanks team. I'll file the incident postmortem with timelines and next steps.

maria: leaving logs and command history in the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:

raj: nice calm response. closing thread once postmortem is up.

sam: will draft the customer-facing summary.

olivia: CS will send follow-up confirming hardening window. :mailbox_with_mail:

ops-lead: good job. closing oncall handoff in 10.

incident-bot: NOTE: please tag this incident in the postmortem tracker: /incidents/3825000000
